Attention Trading Partners: Take Action Now Before MaineCare’s New Online Portal Goes Live

Aug 03, 2026

A refreshed and upgraded MIHMS is coming in mid October 2026. The Office of MaineCare Services (OMS), in partnership with Gainwell Technologies, is launching an upgraded MIHMS, to bring enhanced security, improved usability, and a more modern experience to better support your day-to-day work.

The upgrade will include a new “MaineCare Partner Portal” that will replace what is known today as the “Health PAS Online Portal.” Please note that, until the October go-live, we will continue using the name “Health PAS Online Portal” in communications related to current functionality.

You can read more about the benefits to providers and members on the Health PAS Online Portal.

Trading Partners Preparation

This message is part of a series about changes to how trading partners will access the new portal and what you must do now to prepare for these changes.

Trading partners include providers, billing agents, health plans, clearinghouses, and business associates. Trading partners have an important role to play in supporting a smooth transition and uninterrupted access to the portal after go-live.

Portal Access Impacts and Required Actions Before Go‑Live

The preparation activities and changes below will improve system security by ensuring the right people have the right access, at go-live and ongoing. Most actions are only for Admin (R7) users.

Most important: Providers with duplicate emails need to make changes to their portal user accounts now to assist with account migration to the upgraded portal. On September 1, we will terminate current Admin (R7) user accounts that share an email address with another user account. We will not terminate Admin (R7) user accounts if they are the only Admin (R7) on the Trading Partner account.

If a user account is terminated and they still need portal access, another user with Admin Rights (R7) can invite the terminated user using a unique email address, not the one previously used.

Activity/Change

Your Action

Why it Matters

What’s Next?

At go-live, MaineCare will only migrate Admin (R7) accounts to the new portal.

 

MaineCare will not migrate inactive accounts.

Designate at least one active Admin (R7) per organization, and two for backup coverage.

 

Trading Partners with large user populations should plan for sufficient Admin (R7) coverage to avoid access delays after go-live; we recommend one Admin (R7) per 25 users.

 

Remove inactive Admin (R7) accounts.

After go-live, Admin (R7) users will need to re-invite all other active users. More Admin (R7) users mean less re-invitation work for each user.

 

Trading Partners have an existing and ongoing responsibility to remove inactive users to help keep our systems and data secure.

 

We will monitor the number and activity of Admin (R7) users per Trading Partner and will reach out to individual Trading Partners if needed.

In the new portal, your username will be your email address.

MaineCare will not migrate accounts that share an email address.

Confirm that each active Admin (R7) user account has its own unique email address.

OMS will deactivate accounts that continue to share email addresses as we approach go-live.

After go-live, Admin (R7) users will need immediate access to the portal to invite other users and avoid disruption in Trading Partner work.

We will monitor accounts that share email addresses and will reach out to individual Trading Partners if needed.

Admin (R7) users will invite other users to the portal and designate your roles after go-live.

 

Admin (R7) will be able to choose from ~40 permissions, compared to 9 today.

Prepare to invite users after go-live:

  • Know who needs a user account in the new portal
  • Know the permission level each user will need to have

 

Admin (R7) users will need to invite other users shortly after go-live to avoid a disruption in Trading Partner work.

 

We will share more information during trainings including role definitions, templates, and other guidance.

 

For questions, please email Provider Services or call 1-866-690-5585.

Provider Responsibility Regarding Third Party Liability and Secondary Billing

Aug 03, 2026

In a previous notice, the Office of MaineCare Services (OMS) reminded providers of your responsibilities regarding third -party liability and secondary billing. Pursuant to MaineCare Benefits Manual (MBM) Ch. I Section 1.07-3(B), MaineCare is the payor of last resort. OMS announced that we will update the billing and claims system requirements to accurately reflect the provider’s obligation to bill primary insurance when other coverage is available.

Effective August 10, 2026, our claims system will no longer treat most Current Procedural Terminology (CPT) and Healthcare Common Procedure Coding System (HCPCS) codes as exempt from billing the primary commercial carrier. In accordance with MBM Ch. I Section 1.07: Third Party Liability, providers must seek payment from the primary carrier before billing MaineCare for all claims for these services for members with primary coverage, even when:

  • the billing codes for same services vary between payors; and
  • the primary payor’s service coverage applies only to a portion of the MaineCare defined service. For example, this applies when the MaineCare service is more comprehensive than the primary payor’s coverage.

MaineCare also recognizes that many provider types that were previously unable to enroll in Medicare can now enroll and bill Medicare as the primary payor for services delivered to members dually eligible for Medicare and Medicaid. Providers eligible to enroll with Medicare to deliver Medicare reimbursable services must do so to receive MaineCare reimbursement as a secondary payor.

MaineCare’s claims system will accept an Explanation of Benefits (EOB) with primary dollars attached even if the billing codes differ. The system will process secondary claims as long as the provider, member, dates of service, and billed charges match. Providers must use the most specific code possible to maintain billing integrity and to comply with correct claim submission procedures.

Please monitor MaineCare e-messages for future communications on this topic as continued reviews and necessary system changes occur. We appreciate your efforts to preserve MaineCare funding and ensure compliance with these requirements.

For questions, please contact your Provider Relations Specialist.

To support system readiness activities, MaineCare is temporarily pausing the implementation of configuration changes from the end of August to the end of October.

Requests submitted by August 19, 2026, if approved, will be implemented no later than the last synchronization on August 25, 2026. Continue to submit these requests as usual after these dates. Rate Change Requests

Continue submitting rate change requests as usual to MIHMSRateRqst.DHHS@maine.gov throughout this period. MaineCare will review and document change requests as appropriate for implementation beginning at the end of October.

MaineCare Telehealth Services Provider Licensure Requirements

Aug 04, 2026

As a reminder, all providers delivering telehealth services to MaineCare members must be enrolled with MaineCare and must comply with MaineCare Benefits Manual (MBM) Chapter I, Section 4: Telehealth Services.

Chapter I, Section 4 requires that providers be “appropriately licensed, accredited, certified, and/or registered in the state where the member is located during the provision of the telehealth service.”

This means that all providers delivering in-person or telehealth services to MaineCare members, who are in Maine at the time of the service, must hold appropriate Maine credentials or Interstate Licensure Compacts recognized by the Department of Professional and Financial Regulation (DPFR) or other appropriate organization. 

Pursuant to MBM, Ch. I, Section 1.18 failure to comply with these requirements can result in the denial of claims or recoupment of payment because services delivered without proper state licensure are not eligible for reimbursement.

For questions, please contact your Provider Relations Specialist.

entry.content: Maine Human Rights Commission # 51 State House Station, Augusta, ME 04333-0051 Physical location: 19 Union Street, Augusta, ME 04330 ■ ■Phone (207) 624-6290 Fax (207) 624-8729 TTY: Maine Relay 711 www.maine.gov/mhrc Kit Thomson Crossman Barbara Archer Hirsch EXECUTIVE DIRECTOR COMMISSION COUNSEL MAINE HUMAN RIGHTS COMMISSION Public Guidance Statement RE: HUD's New Emotional Support Animal Enforcement Guidance and Maine Housing Providers' Continuing Obligations Under the Maine Human Rights Act August 4, 2026 What Has Changed at the Federal Level On May 22, 2026, the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) issued an enforcement memorandum announcing that it will no longer find reasonable cause in housing complaints involving emotional support animals (ESAs). In other words, animals that provide comfort, companionship, or otherwise mitigate the effects of a person’s disability but have not been individually trained to perform specific disability-related tasks are no longer protected at the federal level. Going forward, HUD will pursue enforcement only where an animal has been trained to perform work or tasks directly related to a person's disability (essentially, HUD has imported the Americans with Disabilities Act's narrower "service animal" definition into Fair Housing Act enforcement). HUD simultaneously rescinded its 2020 guidance, which had for years provided meaningful protections to individuals who rely on ESAs as part of their disability-related care. After 35 years without updating its regulations in this area, the federal government's chosen solution has been, perhaps unsurprisingly, to reduce protections rather than clarify them. New MaineCare Partner Portal Training for Trading Partners

We previously shared that a refreshed and upgraded MIHMS, with a new “MaineCare Partner Portal,” is coming in October 2026. This will replace the current HealthPAS Online Portal. We are now inviting trading partners to register for training starting September 8, 2026, to help you prepare for the transition to the new portal. 

Gainwell Technologies will be leading live virtual instructor-led training sessions. These courses will provide the knowledge and skills needed to navigate the new portal, complete daily business functions, and use new portal features. Training demonstrations, materials, and supporting resources will help participants prepare for a successful transition.

  • Use the Learning Management System (LMS) registration to create an account, access the training catalog, and enroll in applicable sessions. See the instructions below for guidance in registering.

Competitive Skills Scholarship Program (CSSP) Rule Changes Effective August 2, 2026

August 5, 2026

The Maine Department of Labor has updated the Competitive Skills Scholarship Program (CSSP) rules to implement recent statutory changes, expand participant supports, improve program flexibility, and clarify program requirements. The revised rules took effect on August 2, 2026.

Some of the most significant changes include:

  • Expanded monthly stipend eligibility. More students may now qualify for a monthly CSSP stipend because income eligibility limits have increased.
  • Partial stipends for part-time students. Eligible part-time students may now receive a prorated monthly stipend based on their enrollment status and income.
  • Expanded support services. Eligible participants may qualify for increased assistance with transportation, vehicle repairs, and other necessary needs under higher support service funding limits.
  • Expanded educational opportunities. Eligibility has also been expanded for applicants with pre-existing preparatory associate degree programs.
  • Improved program clarity and accessibility. The revised rules simplify eligibility requirements, clarify appeal rights, improve communication preferences, and increase transparency regarding the High-Wage, In-Demand Occupations list.
  • New CSSP Cohort funding opportunities. Training providers and their partners will be invited to apply for CSSP Cohort funding. The Maine Department of Labor will host a listening session to gather feedback on implementation before issuing a Request for Applications (RFA) for pilot cohort programs.

For those interested in reviewing the complete rule changes, including the final adopted rule, tracked changes, and the Department's Summary of Comments and Responses from the rulemaking process, please visit the Maine Department of Labor Rulemaking webpage: https://www.maine.gov/labor/rulemaking/

CSSP Cohort Listening Session

Community members interested in learning more about the CSSP Cohort model are invited to join a listening session on September 18th, at 10:00 a.m. to share ideas, discuss opportunities to expand access, and help identify implementation priorities.

Zoom Registration: https://mainestate.zoom.us/meeting/register/-vPlt9ZbSG23mGKG96bmsg

Current CSSP participants will receive a separate email describing the rule changes and inviting them to schedule a meeting with their CSSP case manager to review whether they may qualify for additional benefits under the new rules.

Thank you for your continued partnership in helping Maine people access education, training, and employment through the Competitive Skills Scholarship Program.

Maine DEP Issues Air Quality Alert as Particle Pollution Levels Predicted to Escalate to Unhealthy Ranges

Maine Department of Environmental Protection sent this bulletin at 07/17/2026 03:23 PM EDT

--- PRESS RELEASE ---

For Immediate Release

 

Maine DEP Issues Air Quality Alert as Particle Pollution Levels Predicted to Escalate to Unhealthy Ranges

 

AUGUSTA, July 17, 2026 — The Maine Department of Environmental Protection warns that ground-level particle pollution concentrations are forecasted to reach the ‘Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups’ (USG) level this Saturday due to wildfire smoke drifting in from Manitoba and Ontario, Canada.

The smoke plume is expected to move back over Maine during the day on Saturday, with air quality measured by a 24-hour average forecasted at the USG level. Some hours may experience particle pollution levels even higher than this range. Residents are encouraged to follow health recommendations that suit their individual needs.

Smoke conditions may improve by midday Sunday, but due to the unpredictable nature of wildfire smoke, the Maine Department of Environmental Protection advises checking their website or calling the toll-free Air Quality Hotline at 800-223-1196 for the latest updates throughout the weekend.

Elevated particle pollution levels can affect sensitive groups such as children, older adults, outdoor workers, and individuals with respiratory or heart conditions including asthma, bronchitis, and COPD. Symptoms may include coughing, shortness of breath, throat irritation, and mild chest pain. Even healthy adults engaging in outdoor physical activity might notice these effects.

Some actions you can take to protect your health during such periods include:

  • Avoiding strenuous outdoor activity
  • Closing windows and circulating indoor air with a fan or air conditioner
  • Asthmatics should keep their quick-relief medications and action plan handy

Additional health information may be found on the following websites:

  • Maine CDC asthma prevention and control
  • USEPA's asthma control and management
  • AIRNOW for smoke impacted areas

Addition of the TH Modifier to Support National Maternity Care Coding and Reimbursement Changes Effective September 1, 2026

Aug 06, 2026

The American Medical Association (AMA) announced maternity care services code changes that will be effective January 1, 2027. These changes include the removal of 17 billing codes, the addition of 12 billing codes, and revisions to 6 billing codes to reflect modern obstetric practices, allow for more accurate and transparent reporting, and to create a data foundation to better attribute maternal care and support the complexities of team-based care throughout a patient's journey.

In preparation for these changes, MaineCare is also making changes to coding requirements for maternity care services, including the transition to non-global and non-bundled care coding and reimbursement. To ensure consistent reimbursement MaineCare is directing providers to take the following actions no later than prior to September 1, 2026:

  • Adjust maternity care visit billing from global or bundled service codes to Evaluation and Management (E/M) service codes based on each member’s estimated due date and the anticipated number of visits for the remainder of their antepartum period in accordance with AMA Antepartum Transition Reporting guidance;.
  • Append the TH modifier for all maternity care E/M service codes on your claim to identify the visit as a maternity care service;
  • Transition from total-visit tracking to individual encounter documentation, as each prenatal and postpartum visit must now independently support standard E/M complexity or time rules; and
  • Monitor professional guidance from organizations like the American College of Obstetrics and Gynecology and the AMA to prepare billers and systems for the significant coding changes to be effective on January 1, 2027.

As a reminder, providers should also continue to identify and report maternity-related diagnosis codes on all claims submitted to MaineCare, as applicable, to ensure more accurate and transparent data relating to maternity services.   

Please monitor MaineCare e-messages for future updates on this topic.

For questions, please contact your Provider Relations Specialist

Intensive Outpatient Program (IOP) Clinical Eligibility Review and Billing Criteria for Section 45 and 46 Hospitals Update

Aug 10, 2026

Beginning September 1, 2026, IOP services delivered by hospitals enrolled under MaineCare Benefits Manual (MBM) Chapter II, Sections 45 and 46 will require clinical eligibility review and billing criteria in alignment with Medicare’s IOP services billing requirements.  

Effective for dates of service on, or after, September 1, 2026, hospitals delivering IOP services must: 

  1. Submit a clinical review request to Acentra Health before delivering services to determine a MaineCare member’s IOP service eligibility. Members determined to meet clinical eligibility criteria as defined in MBM, Chapter II, Section 65 will receive a Case ID number to authorize billing for the delivery of IOP services by Section 45 and 46 providers. 

  2. With clinical review approval, deliver IOP services in accordance with their hospital licensure and the requirements of MBM, Chapter II, Section 65.05-4.  

  3. Submit claims using the corresponding CPT/HCPCS codes or revenue codes for actual services delivered including modifier(s) as applicable. Condition Code 92 (CC 92) is required in Form Locator fields 18-24. 

  4. Retain the clinical review Case ID number in the member’s medical record. Because IOP services without a clinical review Case ID are not eligible for reimbursement, providers must maintain clinical review approval records for Program Integrity purposes. 

  5. Deliver services in accordance with Division of Licensing and Certification (DLC) requirements.   

Please note: This notice supersedes previous MaineCare Section 45 and 46 IOP billing instructions including, but not limited to, the June 14, 2023 and August 18, 2023 messages.  

Medicare’s claims criteria are outlined in the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) publication, including MLN 13496 – Billing Requirements for Intensive Outpatient Program Services with New Condition Code 92.

For questions regarding hospital licensure requirements for the delivery of IOP services, please reach out to Anna Blackwell, Associate Director of DLC: Medical Facilities Unit.  

For questions regarding IOP service and eligibility standards set forth in Section 65, or the billing requirements for providers enrolled under Sections 45 and 46, please contact Provider Relations Specialist Tiffany Norton.

entry.title: US Department of Labor finds urgent care employer failed to pay over $113K in owed wages to workers for required orientation, meetings, training
entry.content: ATLANTA – The U.S. Department of Labor has recovered $113,199 in back wages after an investigation found a Richmond Hill urgent care facility failed to pay its workers for hours worked and retaliated against a worker for questioning its pay practices.An investigation by the department’s Wage and Hour Division found that Premier Health Consultants LLC – operating as St. Joseph Candler Urgent Care – violated the Fair Labor Standards Act by paying straight time instead of time and one-half in overtime for all hours worked over 40 when employees were required to attend mandatory orientation, meetings, and training. The employer also required certain employees to work off the clock, resulting in unpaid overtime, and suspended a worker who questioned pay practices, all violations of the FLSA.Workers and employers can call the Wage and Hour Division with questions and requests for compliance assistance at its toll-free helpline, 866-4US-WAGE (487-9243). Employers are encouraged to use the agency’s industry-specific compliance assistance toolkits to learn about their responsibilities under the laws enforced by the division. The agency’s PAID program offers employers an opportunity to self-report and resolve potential minimum wage and overtime violations under the FLSA, as well as certain potential violations under the Family and Medical Leave Act. Learn more about the Wage and Hour Division, including a search tool that workers can use if they think they may be owed back wages collected by the division. Download the agency’s free timesheet app for iOS and Android devices to track hours and pay.

Providers whose license is under a Title 5 review may use your Title 5 notice to extend your enrollment with MaineCare in MIHMS by six months, and for every six months thereafter, until the Title 5 review is resolved. Providers must complete this update by submitting a maintenance case via the Health PAS Online Portal. They can use the Provider Maintenance User Guide for step-by-step instructions.

Aug 11, 2026

In cooperation with the Maine Department of Health and Human Services’ Center for Disease Control and Prevention (Maine CDC), officials from U.S. Department of Agriculture’s (USDA) Wildlife Services will distribute oral rabies vaccine (ORV) baits this week. USDA Wildlife Services will distribute nearly 599,000 ORV baits in Aroostook County from August 12 through August 24.

The fall ORV bait distribution follows this past spring’s distribution and is in response to continued rabid raccoon detections in Aroostook County. The USDA’s Wildlife Services spreads ORV baits to reduce the spread of the raccoon rabies virus in Maine. The baits help limit the potential for human and domestic animal exposures to the rabies virus through contact with infected wild animals.

Crews will spread the bait by air in rural areas and by vehicle in more populated areas. Each bait is a fishmeal-coated cube or sachet about one to two inches in size. Although humans and pets cannot get rabies from contact with the bait, they should not touch or move them.

Studies show that ORV baits are safe in many species of animals, including domestic dogs and cats. While dogs may get upset stomachs if they eat a lot of bait, there are no known long-term health risks. If a person has skin contact with a bait cube or sachet, rinse the affected area with warm water and soap. For concerns about a person or pet touching or eating a bait, call the Maine CDC’s 24-hour line at 800-821-5821.

Since 2003, the USDA’s Wildlife Services has worked to halt the spread of raccoon rabies in northern Maine. They also collaborate with Canadian officials in New Brunswick and Quebec to reduce the presence of rabies across Maine and Canada. The ORV bait distribution program in Maine is part of a larger effort by the USDA’s Wildlife Services to prevent the westward spread of raccoon rabies. This effort creates a barrier along the Appalachian Mountains from the Canadian border to Alabama.

Rabies is a virus that infects the nervous system of humans and other mammals. It spreads mainly through a bite from an infected animal. Once symptoms develop, rabies is almost always fatal. Timely post-exposure treatment can prevent disease in people. Approximately 90 percent of reported animal rabies cases in the U.S. occur in wildlife. As of August 10, 2026, 28 animals tested positive for rabies this year in 12 counties across Maine. These animals include raccoons, skunks, foxes, bats, and a goat.

To help protect yourself and your pet against rabies:

  • Keep your pets and livestock up to date on rabies vaccinations.
  • Feed pets indoors.
  • Keep garbage cans or other sources of food tightly secured.
  • Do not feed, touch, or adopt wild animals. Be cautious of stray dogs and cats.
  • Do not move wildlife. This can spread rabies into new areas.
  • Wash bite or scratch wounds with soap and water for 10 to 15 minutes.

Who to contact:

  • If an animal bites or scratches you, contact a health care provider.
  • If an animal bites or scratches your pet, contact your veterinarian.
  • To report a dead or suspicious-acting animal in northern Maine, contact the USDA’s Wildlife Services. In other parts of Maine, contact the nearest Maine Regional Communications Dispatch Center.

For more information:

  • USDA Rabies webpage
  • Maine CDC Rabies webpage
  • USDA Wildlife Services: 1-866-487-3297
  • Maine CDC disease reporting & consultation line: 1-800-821-5821 (available 24/7)

entry.title: Maine CDC: Childhood Vaccine Guidance Remains Unchanged Following Federal Action
entry.content:
Aug 11, 2026

Maine will continue to follow the guidance of the American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP) on childhood vaccine recommendations, despite President Donald Trump’s executive order on childhood vaccinations, per the Maine Department of Health and Human Services’ Center for Disease Control and Prevention (Maine CDC).

“President Trump and Secretary Kennedy are playing politics with the lives of our nation’s children. Vaccines are safe and effective and save lives,” said Governor Janet Mills. “Maine will continue to follow the science and the facts, and our approach to vaccines remains unchanged by yesterday’s executive order.” 

“Vaccines are our most effective defense against vaccine-preventable illnesses,” said Dr. Puthiery Va, Director of the Maine CDC.“In Maine, vaccines remain available at no cost to eligible children through the Maine CDC’s Immunization Program. Maine’s school and child care immunization requirements remain unchanged by federal actions to date.”

As the AAP has noted in their 8/10 statement in response to this executive order:

 “Vaccine recommendations from the American Academy of Pediatrics are tailored to the health of children living in the United States and are based on decades of research and systematic tracking of real-world experiences. Pediatricians recommend children receive certain vaccines at specific ages based on when children's immune systems will respond best and when they are most vulnerable to certain diseases. Sometimes this means children will receive a single shot that protects against multiple diseases, or they may receive multiple vaccines at one visit.” 

Beginning in 2021, Maine removed non-medical exemptions from the school and child care immunization requirements pursuant Public Law 2019, Ch. 154. That decision was upheld by a vote of 72.81 percent of Maine voters at the ballot box in 2020.

MAINE- The State Workforce Development Board (SWDB) - https://www.maine.gov/swb/board/index.shtml announced the launch of Maine's Workforce Pell Application - https://www.worksourcemaine.com/pages/workforce-pell , providing eligible Title IV postsecondary institutions with an online process to seek approval to offer Workforce Pell-eligible programs.

Workforce Pell expands federal Pell Grant eligibility to approved short-term workforce training programs that prepare students for high-skill, high-wage, and in-demand careers. entry.title: Continuing the Fight Against the Opioid Epidemic
entry.content:
Hello, this is Governor Janet Mills, and thank you for listening.

Over the five years leading up to 2019, more than 1,600 people in Maine died from drug overdoses. We were losing a person every day. About 8% of all babies in Maine were born substance-exposed—that's three each day. The life-saving drug Naloxone was not generally available. There were few treatment beds, and when someone was ready to get into recovery, even fewer treatment options were available if they didn't have health insurance.

When I took office, I knew that what Maine had been doing for so many years just wasn't working. We needed a coordinated response that broke down the silos of government, set aside the stigma, and spoke out about every aspect of the opioid epidemic. I promised that we would put the full force of my Administration behind the families who lost loved ones, the businesses who lost employees, and all the communities that have been diminished by this public health crisis. 

So my first executive order, signed on my first day in office, fulfilled the will of the people of Maine and expanded MaineCare to more than 90,000 people. Today, nearly 40,000 people receive treatment for substance use disorder through MaineCare. Expanding health insurance was a critical first step to confronting the opioid crisis.

I named Gordon Smith as my Director of Opioid Response, and I signed the second executive order with basic strategies and specific action steps. That order established a Prevention and Recovery Cabinet made up of commissioners from 14 government agencies and the Attorney General's Office and the Judicial Branch.

We outlined key steps to preventing overdoses and deaths, including making Naloxone widely available statewide, and since early 2019, we've distributed more than 870,000 doses of Naloxone, which has saved thousands of lives.

We then outlined steps to expand effective treatment and recovery measures, including training 250 recovery coaches and funding recovery coaches in ten emergency departments. Now we've trained more than 4,000 individuals as recovery coaches, and we've increased the number of certified recovery residences from 11 to 119.

We've created youth recovery coaching programs in Hancock and Washington counties in the schools, creating peer-to-peer connections that can give a young person the hope to face the future. And we held statewide trainings and leadership conferences, which taught more than 400 youth how to create positive change in their communities. 

We created TreatmentConnection.com, a one-stop-shop for individuals seeking treatment that allows them to find out in real time what there is available for behavioral health services among more than 500 providers. Since that went live in 2025, TreatmentConnection has been used 8,000 times.

We're also increasing good-paying jobs for people in recovery, rewarding businesses who understand the unique experiences of people in recovery. And we've created the Recovery Friendly Workplaces designation, a certification held by 86 businesses who employ nearly 25,000 people statewide.

You know, we're not giving up on interdiction as well, making sure we take drugs off the street as much as possible to keep people from becoming addicted in the first place. My Administration is doing what we can in a responsible manner to stop deadly drugs from reaching Maine, to prevent substance abuse in the first place, to treat it when we can't prevent it, to set people on a lifelong path to recovery, and, above all else, to save lives.

From January to June of this year, fatal overdoses decreased by nearly 9% in Maine. This is the fourth consecutive year of declining overdose deaths. And that's welcome news, but we know we can't be complacent. Every overdose is a tragic and, I believe, preventable loss of a valued life. So let's all recommit to supporting people as they start, stumble, or resume their recovery, and to responding to new phases of the opioid epidemic to save lives.

This is Governor Janet Mills, and thank you for listening.

Save-the-Date: DHHS Partner Briefing on Federal Medicaid Work Requirements and Increased Renewals

Aug 14, 2026

DHHS Partner Briefing on Federal Medicaid Work Requirements and Increased Renewals 

When: Monday, August 24, 2026, 3:00 – 4:30 PM 

Where: Virtual, please register in advance. 

You are invited to join a Maine Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS) briefing to learn about plans to implement federal changes to Medicaid (in Maine, MaineCare) eligibility that will go into effect on January 1, 2027.   

During this webinar, the DHHS Office for Family Independence (OFI) and Office of MaineCare Services (OMS) will provide an overview of upcoming changes to MaineCare eligibility for Expansion Adults: 

  • New Work Requirements;  

  • Coverage renewals every 6 months instead of every 12 months; and 

  • Retroactive coverage of 1 month instead of 3 months. 

MaineCare Expansion members are adults between 19 and 64 years old who get MaineCare based on their income. They do not meet the Social Security disability guidelines or have Medicare. OFI and OMS will also provide an update on planning for implementation and communications.   

We are also pleased to share the Partner Communications Toolkit, which can be found at MaineCare.gov/work. This toolkit includes materials you can download and print or include in your digital and social media channels to reach the populations in your community that will need to know more and take action to meet the new federal Work Requirements for Medicaid.  

Important Timelines to Note:  

  • August 14, 2026: Launch of Federal Changes and Work Requirements webpages, and Partner Toolkit launch – first phase  

  • August 24, 2026: Partner briefing focused on what to know 

  • Beginning August 19, 2026: OFI will send knowledge building letters and text messages to MaineCare Expansion Adults 

  • Fall 2026: Continued communication and partnership with providers and community partners.  

  • Late 2026 and through 2027: OFI will provide direct 1:1 phone call outreach to impacted MaineCare Expansion Adults ahead of their renewal month. 

  • January 2027 and forward: MaineCare Expansion Adults will need to meet Work Requirements starting with their first renewal in 2027 and will have 6-month renewals from that point on. 

Register and join to learn more and assist with sharing information and resources in your community.     

After registering, you will receive a confirmation email containing information about joining the meeting. Feel free to share this invitation with other interested organizations who may wish to attend.   

Space is limited, so please register early.
